members.name: Gordon Stoker (present at initial RCA sessions)

podcast.title: Initial Exclusion and Elvis's Demand
podcast.body: Only Gordon Stoker, one member of The Jordanaires, was present at Elvis's initial RCA sessions. The full group was not hired due to Steve Sholes' cost-cutting measure of using RCA-signed artists (The Speer Family). Elvis later insisted that all The Jordanaires be employed for his future sessions. "When Elvis found out at a later session that this had happened as a cost-cutting measure, he insisted that all the Jordanaires be employed at his future sessions."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Male Nashville Session Vocalists
podcast.body: This male vocal group served as the equivalent of the Anita Kerr Singers, providing backing vocals for Nashville sessions that required male voices. "the male equivalent was the Jordan Ares."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 83: "Only the Lonely" by Roy Orbison

podcast.title: Primary Backing Group for Elvis
podcast.body: The Jordanaires were the group that backed Elvis Presley throughout the 1950s and 1960s. "the group who would back Elvis throughout the 50s and 60s."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Provided Backing Vocals for Janice Martin
podcast.body: The Jordanaires, known for their work with Elvis Presley, also provided backing vocals on at least some of Janice Martin's records, further aligning her sound with Elvis's. "on at least some of her records, the Jordanaires provided backing vocals as they did for Elvis."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 40: "Drugstore Rock 'n' Roll" by Janis Martin

podcast.title: Tharp's Tour Mates
podcast.body: This white vocal group toured with Sister Rosetta Tharp, but failed to understand the necessity of her having her own bus in segregated America, simply thinking it was "cool." They later gained fame backing Elvis. "even when Tharp toured with a white vocal group, the Jordan airs, who would later find more fame backing up some country singer named Elvis something."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
